components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 违 is to go against or part from.
韦 (wéi) gives the sound exactly: 违 wéi, also in 围 wéi and 伟 wěi.
又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.

example.hanzi: 这样做违反了公司的规定。
example.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò wéifǎn le gōngsī de guīdìng.
example.english: Doing this violates the company's rules.
example.fact: 违反 almost always takes an abstract, rule-like object — a law, regulation, or principle (违反规定, "violate a rule") — while for physically breaking a concrete object, Chinese uses an entirely different verb, 打破 or 弄坏, a split English "violate" vs. "break" does not map onto directly.

examples.hanzi: 开车闯红灯是违反交通规则的。
examples.pinyin: Kāi chē chuǎng hóngdēng shì wéifǎn jiāotōng guīzé de.
examples.english: Running a red light violates traffic rules.

examples.hanzi: 违反规定的人要受到处罚。
examples.pinyin: Wéifǎn guīdìng de rén yào shòudào chǔfá.
examples.english: People who violate the rules will be punished.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks mounds and steps, as in 院, 队, 附, 陆; 阶 is a stair step.
介 (jiè) hints at the sound: 阶 jiē is close to 界 jiè and 价 jià.
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand with a tool striking, as in 毁, 殴; 段 is a piece cut off a larger whole, and sounds out 锻 duàn.

example.hanzi: 这个项目已经进入了新的阶段。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yǐjīng jìnrù le xīn de jiēduàn.
example.english: This project has already entered a new stage.
example.fact: 阶 (from 阝, "hill," plus a phonetic 介) originally referred to physical steps cut into a hillside, and 段 pictures a hand-held tool 殳 cutting something into a segment — 阶段 fuses "a step" with "a segment" into the abstract idea of one stage within a longer process.

examples.hanzi: 孩子在不同的阶段需要不同的教育。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zài bù tóng de jiēduàn xūyào bù tóng de jiàoyù.
examples.english: Children need different education at different stages.

examples.hanzi: 这是工作的第一个阶段。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōngzuò de dì-yī ge jiēduàn.
examples.english: This is the first phase of the work.

components.note: 不 (bù) is a loose sound clue for fǒu and gives the meaning "not".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: saying no.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".

example.hanzi: 他否认自己做过这件事。
example.pinyin: Tā fǒurèn zìjǐ zuòguo zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: He denied having done this.
example.fact: 否认 is built from 否 ("no, not so") plus 认 ("to acknowledge, recognize") — literally "to not-acknowledge" — and its near-opposite 承认 ("to admit, confess") swaps in 承 ("to bear, undertake") for the same 认 root, giving a matched pair of deny/admit verbs built the same way.

examples.hanzi: 他否认了所有的指控。
examples.pinyin: Tā fǒurèn le suǒyǒu de zhǐkòng.
examples.english: He denied all the charges.

examples.hanzi: 没有人能否认她的才华。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén néng fǒurèn tā de cáihuá.
examples.english: No one can deny her talent.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun sinking into the grass: dusk (the original of 暮 mù); later borrowed for "no, do not". 莫 also sounds out 墓 mù, 幕 mù and 摸 mō.

example.hanzi: 莫非他生病了?
example.pinyin: Mòfēi tā shēngbìng le?
example.english: Could it be that he is ill?
example.fact: 莫 was originally 'dusk' (the sun setting in the grass), and the later character 暮 took over that meaning. As a word it is a classical 'not/no one' that survives in 莫非 (could it be), 莫名其妙 (baffling) and 莫斯科 (Moscow).

examples.hanzi: 这件事你莫要告诉别人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ mò yào gàosu biérén.
examples.english: Don't tell anyone about this.

examples.hanzi: 他莫名其妙地哭了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā mòmíng qímiào de kū le qǐlái.
examples.english: He started crying for no reason.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 我们得好好商量一下这件事。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen děi hǎohǎo shāngliang yíxià zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: We need to discuss this matter carefully.
example.fact: 商量 implies a mutual, back-and-forth negotiation between two or more people working toward a joint decision — closer to English "to talk something over" than the more one-directional 讨论 ("to discuss, debate"), which can just as easily describe one person analyzing a topic alone.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我想和你商量一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ xiǎng hé nǐ shāngliang yíxià.
examples.english: I'd like to discuss this matter with you.

examples.hanzi: 他们正在商量去哪里度假。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhèngzài shāngliang qù nǎlǐ dùjià.
examples.english: They are talking over where to go on vacation.

components.note: 十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.hanzi: 桌子上有书、笔什么的。
example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu shū, bǐ shénme de.
example.english: There are books, pens, and so on, on the table.
example.fact: 什么的 always closes out a list rather than opening one, tacked onto the final item to mean "...and so on" — functioning much like English "etc.," but built from two pieces reused elsewhere with unrelated senses: the question word 什么 ("what") and the particle 的.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢吃面条、饺子什么的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī miàntiáo, jiǎozi shénmede.
examples.english: I like eating noodles, dumplings and the like.

examples.hanzi: 出门要带钥匙、钱包什么的。
examples.pinyin: Chūmén yào dài yàoshi, qiánbāo shénmede.
examples.english: When you go out, bring your keys, wallet and so on.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 他这么做完全是出于好意。
example.pinyin: Tā zhème zuò wánquán shì chūyú hǎoyì.
example.english: He did this entirely out of good intentions.
example.fact: 出于 always names a motive or origin right after it — 出于好意 ("out of good intentions"), 出于礼貌 ("out of politeness") — pairing the verb 出 ("to come out of") with the preposition 于 ("from, at") into a fixed phrase that works much like English "out of" before a reason.

examples.hanzi: 她这样做是出于对朋友的关心。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèyàng zuò shì chūyú duì péngyou de guānxīn.
examples.english: She did this out of concern for her friend.

examples.hanzi: 出于安全考虑，请系好安全带。
examples.pinyin: Chūyú ānquán kǎolǜ, qǐng jì hǎo ānquándài.
examples.english: For safety reasons, please fasten your seat belt.

components.note: 艹 (grass, 草字头) — marks plants and herbs, as in 花 flower, 草 grass, 菜 vegetable; 蒙 is covering, like grass over something; also méng, Mongolia.

example.hanzi: 她用手蒙住了眼睛。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu méngzhù le yǎnjing.
example.english: She covered her eyes with her hands.
example.fact: 蒙 is méng for 'cover' (蒙面, 启蒙 'enlightenment', 蒙受 'to suffer, receive'). Read mēng it means to trick or guess, as in 蒙人 and 蒙对了. Read Měng, it is the Mongols: 蒙古 (Mongolia).

examples.hanzi: 蒙蒙细雨下了一整天。
examples.pinyin: Méngméng xìyǔ xià le yì zhěng tiān.
examples.english: A fine drizzle fell all day.

examples.hanzi: 他被人蒙骗了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi rén méngpiàn le.
examples.english: He was deceived by someone.

components.note: 立 (stand) — the person-standing radical, as in 站 itself and 位 position; here it carries the meaning of standing.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound exactly: 站 zhàn, also in 战 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 警察大喊:“站住!”
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá dà hǎn: “Zhànzhù!”
example.english: The police shouted, "Stop!"
example.fact: 住 attached after a verb often marks that an action holds firmly in place — 站住 ("stop and stay put," literally "stand-hold"), 记住 ("to remember," literally "remember-hold") — a common verb-complement pattern where 住 contributes "staying fixed" rather than its literal sense "to live, reside."

examples.hanzi: 我一说话，他就站住了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yì shuō huà, tā jiù zhànzhù le.
examples.english: As soon as I spoke, he stopped.

examples.hanzi: 路太滑，我差点没站住。
examples.pinyin: Lù tài huá, wǒ chàdiǎn méi zhànzhù.
examples.english: The road was so slippery that I almost couldn't keep my footing.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — a picture of an ox's head with horns; as a radical it marks cattle, in 牺, 牲, 牧, 物.
亻 (person) — person radical, used for 仔 as "small creature or child", as in 牛仔 cowboy and 仔细 careful.
子 (zǐ) — same sound — 仔 is zǐ; 子 also means child, so sound and meaning agree.

example.hanzi: 电影里的牛仔骑着马进了城。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de niúzǎi qízhe mǎ jìn le chéng.
example.english: The cowboy in the movie rode into town on his horse.
example.fact: 牛仔 literally means "cattle kid" (牛, "cattle" + 仔, "young one, kid") — a fittingly literal name for someone who herds cattle for a living — and the same word, shortened, gives 牛仔裤 ("cowboy pants," i.e. jeans) and 牛仔布 ("denim").

examples.hanzi: 他穿着牛仔裤，真像个西部牛仔。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe niúzǎikù, zhēn xiàng ge xībù niúzǎi.
examples.english: He wears jeans and looks just like a western cowboy.

examples.hanzi: 这个牛仔每天都要照顾几百头牛。
examples.pinyin: Zhège niúzǎi měi tiān dōu yào zhàogù jǐ bǎi tóu niú.
examples.english: This cowboy looks after hundreds of cattle every day.

components.note: 尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 我的朋友尼克来自美国。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou Níkè láizì Měiguó.
example.english: My friend Nick is from America.
example.fact: 尼克 is a pure phonetic transliteration of the English name "Nick" — neither 尼 nor 克 contributes any of its own meaning here, the same way 克 is reused purely for its sound in other transliterated names in this batch, like 克莱尔 ("Claire").

examples.hanzi: 尼克每天骑车去上班。
examples.pinyin: Níkè měi tiān qí chē qù shàngbān.
examples.english: Nick bikes to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 你认识尼克吗？他是新来的同事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Níkè ma? Tā shì xīn lái de tóngshì.
examples.english: Do you know Nick? He is the new coworker.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 香 originally combined grain with 甘 (sweet): the smell of cooked grain, in modern writing 日 stands in for 甘.
木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 桥; 槟 is the areca/betel palm (香槟 is borrowed for champagne).
宾 (bīn) gives the sound exactly: 槟 bīn, also in 滨 bīn and 缤 bīn.

example.hanzi: 他们打开了一瓶香槟庆祝。
example.pinyin: Tāmen dǎkāi le yì píng xiāngbīn qìngzhù.
example.english: They opened a bottle of champagne to celebrate.
example.fact: 香槟 is a phono-semantic loanword: 槟 was chosen mainly to approximate the sound "-pagne" (bīn), while 香 ("fragrant") fits the drink's aroma — a common strategy in Chinese for borrowing foreign words, blending sound-matching with a sense-appropriate character.

examples.hanzi: 新年的时候，大家一起喝了香槟。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián de shíhou, dàjiā yìqǐ hē le xiāngbīn.
examples.english: At New Year, everyone drank champagne together.

examples.hanzi: 婚礼上，朋友们举起香槟祝福新人。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shang, péngyoumen jǔ qǐ xiāngbīn zhùfú xīnrén.
examples.english: At the wedding, friends raised their champagne glasses to bless the newlyweds.

meanings: to steal and make off with

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.hanzi: 有人把我的自行车偷走了。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén bǎ wǒ de zìxíngchē tōuzǒu le.
example.english: Someone stole my bicycle.
example.fact: 走 attached after a verb often marks "away, off" as the direction the action carries something — 偷走 ("to steal away"), 拿走 ("to take away") — a directional-complement pattern that turns a plain verb into "verb + and remove it," distinct from 走 standing alone to mean simply "to walk."

examples.hanzi: 小偷偷走了我的手机。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu tōuzǒu le wǒ de shǒujī.
examples.english: A thief stole my phone.

examples.hanzi: 谁偷走了我桌上的巧克力？
examples.pinyin: Shéi tōuzǒu le wǒ zhuō shang de qiǎokèlì?
examples.english: Who made off with the chocolate on my desk?

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — 艺 originally meant planting and cultivating, later skill and art.
乙 (yǐ) — near sound — 艺 is yì, same syllable with another tone.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 他从小就想成为一名艺术家。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng yìshùjiā.
example.english: Ever since he was little, he's wanted to become an artist.
example.fact: 家 as a suffix meaning "an expert or practitioner of X" turns 艺术 ("art") into 艺术家 ("artist"), the same pattern behind 科学家 ("scientist") and 音乐家 ("musician") — a more prestigious-sounding suffix than the plainer 师 seen elsewhere in this batch, as in 设计师 ("designer").

examples.hanzi: 这位艺术家的作品很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìshùjiā de zuòpǐn hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This artist's works are very famous.

examples.hanzi: 艺术家需要有丰富的想象力。
examples.pinyin: Yìshùjiā xūyào yǒu fēngfù de xiǎngxiànglì.
examples.english: Artists need a rich imagination.

components.note: 尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 外面很冷,快到屋里来吧。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, kuài dào wūlǐ lái ba.
example.english: It's cold outside, come inside quickly.
example.fact: 屋里 attaches the locational suffix 里 ("inside") directly to 屋 ("room, house") to mean "indoors" — the same 里 that turns 这 into 这里 ("here") elsewhere in this deck, here doing the same job of turning a plain noun into a place word.

examples.hanzi: 屋里很暖和，外面在下雪。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo, wàimiàn zài xià xuě.
examples.english: It's warm inside, while it's snowing outside.

examples.hanzi: 屋里没有人，门却开着。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ méiyǒu rén, mén què kāi zhe.
examples.english: There was nobody in the house, but the door was open.

components.note: 兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
艹 (grass, plants) — plant radical for herbs and greens, as in 花, 草, 菜; 莱 originally named a weed.
来 (lái) — same sound as 莱 — handy since 莱 mostly appears in foreign names like 好莱坞.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 克莱尔是我们班最聪明的学生。
example.pinyin: Kèláiěr shì wǒmen bān zuì cōngmíng de xuésheng.
example.english: Claire is the smartest student in our class.
example.fact: Each syllable of 克莱尔 was chosen purely to approximate the English name "Claire" phonetically — none of the three characters' own literal meanings ("to overcome," a weedy plant, an old pronoun) has anything to do with the name itself, a hallmark of Chinese transliterated foreign names.

examples.hanzi: 克莱尔住在巴黎，会说三种语言。
examples.pinyin: Kèlái'ěr zhù zài Bālí, huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.
examples.english: Claire lives in Paris and speaks three languages.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天给克莱尔写了一封信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān gěi Kèlái'ěr xiě le yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: I wrote a letter to Claire yesterday.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 技 is hand skill.
支 (zhī) is a loose sound clue; same part in 枝 zhī and 肢 zhī.
工 (work, craft) — craft and skill — clever handiwork; also in 左, 差.
丂 (kǎo) — near sound — 巧 qiǎo; 丂 also sounds out 考 kǎo and 烤 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 弹好这首曲子需要一些技巧。
example.pinyin: Tán hǎo zhè shǒu qǔzi xūyào yìxiē jìqiǎo.
example.english: Playing this piece well requires some technique.
example.fact: 技巧 leans toward a practiced, hands-on skill or trick of the craft — a musician's fingering, a photographer's framing — while its broader cousin 技术 ("technology, technique") covers systematic, often more formally trained expertise, a distinction that does not survive translation into the single English word "skill."

examples.hanzi: 学外语有很多小技巧。
examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ yǒu hěn duō xiǎo jìqiǎo.
examples.english: There are many little tricks to learning a foreign language.

examples.hanzi: 他的开车技巧非常好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de kāi chē jìqiǎo fēicháng hǎo.
examples.english: His driving skill is very good.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 这首诗表达了作者深厚的情感。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu shī biǎodá le zuòzhě shēnhòu de qínggǎn.
example.english: This poem expresses the poet's deep emotion.
example.fact: 情感 leans toward a more literary or analytical register than the everyday, spoken 感情 — the two characters simply swap order — much as English sometimes prefers "affect" over "feelings" in a clinical or academic context.

examples.hanzi: 他很少表达自己的情感。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shǎo biǎodá zìjǐ de qínggǎn.
examples.english: He rarely expresses his feelings.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影里的情感非常真实。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ de qínggǎn fēicháng zhēnshí.
examples.english: The emotion in this movie is very real.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
大 (person) standing in the middle of a frame 冂 — the idea of the centre (中央); 央 yāng also sounds out 殃 yāng and 秧 yāng.

example.hanzi: 那张桌子放在房间的中央。
example.pinyin: Nà zhāng zhuōzi fàng zài fángjiān de zhōngyāng.
example.english: That table is placed in the center of the room.
example.fact: 中央 can name either a literal physical center (房间的中央, "the center of the room") or the central government or leadership of an organization (中央政府) — a split that English marks by capitalizing "Central" only in the second, institutional sense.

examples.hanzi: 广场的中央有一个大喷泉。
examples.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng de zhōngyāng yǒu yí ge dà pēnquán.
examples.english: There is a big fountain in the middle of the square.

examples.hanzi: 中央电视台的节目很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngyāng Diànshìtái de jiémù hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: Programs on China Central Television are very popular.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 有人提议下周去爬山。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén tíyì xià zhōu qù páshān.
example.english: Someone proposed going hiking next week.
example.fact: 提议 pairs 提 ("to lift, raise") with 议 ("to discuss, deliberate") for a literal "to raise for discussion" — it works as both a verb ("to propose") and a noun ("a proposal") with no change in form, the same free verb/noun flexibility seen in 工作 in the pilot batch.

examples.hanzi: 我提议今晚大家一起吃火锅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tíyì jīnwǎn dàjiā yìqǐ chī huǒguō.
examples.english: I suggest we all have hot pot together tonight.

examples.hanzi: 大家都同意他的提议。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu tóngyì tā de tíyì.
examples.english: Everyone agreed to his proposal.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 逃; 避 is stepping aside.
辟 (bì) — same sound — 避 is bì, like 辟; 辟 also sounds out 壁 bì and 臂 bì.

example.hanzi: 他总是逃避责任。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì táobì zérèn.
example.english: He always avoids responsibility.
example.fact: 逃避 doubles up two verbs that both mean roughly "to flee, avoid" — 逃 ("to escape, flee") and 避 ("to avoid, dodge") — with a slightly disapproving tone, unlike the neutral 避免 ("to avoid"), making 逃避 the word of choice specifically for shirking a duty or facing something one should confront.

examples.hanzi: 你不能一直逃避问题。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng yìzhí táobì wèntí.
examples.english: You can't keep avoiding the problem.

examples.hanzi: 他逃避了老师的问题，什么也没说。
examples.pinyin: Tā táobì le lǎoshī de wèntí, shénme yě méi shuō.
examples.english: He dodged the teacher's question and said nothing.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 我们每周去一次超市。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měi zhōu qù yí cì chāoshì.
example.english: We go to the supermarket once a week.
example.fact: 每 ("each, every") attaches to a whole family of time-unit words the same way — 每天 ("every day"), 每月 ("every month"), 每周 ("every week") — a single, reusable prefix standing in for English's separate constructions "every day/week/month."

examples.hanzi: 我每周都和朋友打一次球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi zhōu dōu hé péngyou dǎ yí cì qiú.
examples.english: Every week I play a ball game with friends.

examples.hanzi: 每周一我们都要开会。
examples.pinyin: Měi zhōu yī wǒmen dōu yào kāihuì.
examples.english: We have a meeting every Monday.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 他因盗窃罪名被捕。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn dàoqiè zuìmíng bèi bǔ.
example.english: He was arrested on a charge of theft.
example.fact: 罪 pictures a net 罒 closing over wrongdoing 非, and 名 pictures calling out with the mouth 口 in the dark 夕 to identify someone — 罪名 fuses "the crime" with "the name for it" into the formal legal term for a specific charge, distinct from 罪 alone, which can mean the broader concept of guilt or sin.

examples.hanzi: 他被指控犯有诈骗罪名。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng fàn yǒu zhàpiàn zuìmíng.
examples.english: He was accused of the charge of fraud.

examples.hanzi: 没有证据，就不能随便给人加罪名。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu zhèngjù, jiù bù néng suíbiàn gěi rén jiā zuìmíng.
examples.english: Without evidence, you can't simply pin a charge on someone.

components.note: 行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.
匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.

example.hanzi: 这个街区最近新开了不少餐厅。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiēqū zuìjìn xīn kāi le bù shǎo cāntīng.
example.english: A lot of new restaurants have opened in this neighborhood recently.
example.fact: 街区 combines 街 ("street") with 区 ("district, zone") into a unit of urban geography roughly matching the English "city block" or "neighborhood" — a distinctly modern, planning-oriented word, unlike the older, more conversational 街上 ("on the street") for describing the same physical space.

examples.hanzi: 我们这个街区很安静。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhège jiēqū hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: Our neighborhood is very quiet.

examples.hanzi: 你的家在哪个街区？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de jiā zài nǎge jiēqū?
examples.english: Which neighborhood is your home in?

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 顶 top, 题 topic, 额 forehead; 频 pairs it with repeating motion for 'again and again'.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 你最喜欢看哪个频道?
example.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan kàn nǎge píndào?
example.english: Which channel do you like watching the most?
example.fact: 频道 was coined for broadcast technology by combining 频 ("frequency," from radio-wave frequency) with 道 ("path, way," the same 道 that underlies 知道 in the pilot batch) — literally "a frequency path," giving Chinese its own compositional word for "channel" rather than a phonetic loan.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸喜欢看新闻频道。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba xǐhuan kàn xīnwén píndào.
examples.english: My dad likes watching the news channel.

examples.hanzi: 你能帮我换一下频道吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ huàn yíxià píndào ma?
examples.english: Can you help me change the channel?

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.hanzi: 这是历史上一个重要的时期。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì lìshǐ shàng yí gè zhòngyào de shíqī.
example.english: This is an important period in history.
example.fact: 时期 names a stretch of history or a broader era (历史时期, "historical period") in a more formal, written register than the everyday 时候 seen in the pilot batch, which almost always marks one specific personal moment inside a "...的时候" clause rather than a sweeping span of time.

examples.hanzi: 这是他一生中最难忘的时期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā yìshēng zhōng zuì nánwàng de shíqī.
examples.english: This was the most unforgettable period of his life.

examples.hanzi: 青春期是孩子成长的重要时期。
examples.pinyin: Qīngchūnqī shì háizi chéngzhǎng de zhòngyào shíqī.
examples.english: Adolescence is an important period in a child's growth.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.

example.hanzi: 请不要在公共场所大声说话。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ dàshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: Please don't talk loudly in public places.
example.fact: 公 alone already carries the sense "fair, shared, not private" (as in 公平, "fair"), and 共 alone means "together, joint" — 公共 doubles up two overlapping "shared" characters into the modern adjective "public," the same reinforcing word-building strategy behind 喜欢 in the pilot batch.

examples.hanzi: 我每天坐公共汽车上班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zuò gōnggòng qìchē shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the public bus to work every day.

examples.hanzi: 公共场所不能抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bù néng chōuyān.
examples.english: Smoking is not allowed in public places.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买; 质 is the real value or substance of something.

example.hanzi: 水是生命必需的物质。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ shì shēngmìng bìxū de wùzhì.
example.english: Water is a substance essential to life.
example.fact: 物质 covers both the scientific sense "matter, substance" and the everyday sense "material things, material comfort" (as in 物质生活, "material life") — a single word spanning a chemistry classroom and a conversation about worldly possessions, where English keeps "matter" and "material" further apart.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的物质生活很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de wùzhì shēnghuó hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: Material life in this city is very rich.

examples.hanzi: 空气中含有多种物质。
examples.pinyin: Kōngqì zhōng hányǒu duō zhǒng wùzhì.
examples.english: The air contains many kinds of substances.

meanings: to repeat from mouth to mouth

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 这是一个古老的传说。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè gǔlǎo de chuánshuō.
example.english: This is an ancient legend.
example.fact: 传说 literally means "to pass on by speaking" (传, "to transmit" + 说, "to speak") — as a noun it names the legend itself, and placed at the start of a sentence (传说..., "legend has it that...") it introduces a claim whose source is folklore rather than verified fact.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶喜欢给我讲古老的传说。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai xǐhuan gěi wǒ jiǎng gǔlǎo de chuánshuō.
examples.english: Grandma likes to tell me ancient legends.

examples.hanzi: 传说，这座山里住着一条龙。
examples.pinyin: Chuánshuō, zhè zuò shān lǐ zhù zhe yì tiáo lóng.
examples.english: Legend has it that a dragon lives in this mountain.

components.note: 身 (body, bow) — 身 is a worn-down picture of a bow, with a hand 寸 drawing it — 射 is to shoot.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 他在射击比赛中获得了第一名。
example.pinyin: Tā zài shèjī bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì yī míng.
example.english: He won first place in the shooting competition.
example.fact: 射 already pictures the whole action on its own — 身 (a drawn bow) and 寸 (a hand releasing it) — so 击 ("to strike, hit") mostly reinforces the sense of forceful impact; 射击 as a compound is reserved for firearms and target shooting, distinct from 射 alone, which also covers shooting an arrow or, more abstractly, casting a glance.

examples.hanzi: 他每周都去练习射击。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu qù liànxí shèjī.
examples.english: He goes to practice shooting every week.

examples.hanzi: 运动员瞄准目标，开始射击。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòngyuán miáozhǔn mùbiāo, kāishǐ shèjī.
examples.english: The athlete aimed at the target and began to shoot.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a person kneeling at food 皀, about to eat: right at hand, immediately; compare 既, who has already eaten.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 即便下雨,我们也要出发。
example.pinyin: Jíbiàn xiàyǔ, wǒmen yě yào chūfā.
example.english: Even if it rains, we still have to set out.
example.fact: 即便 is always the setup half of a two-part sentence completed by 也 ("still, also") — 即便...,也... — functioning as a more formal, written-register synonym for the everyday 就算...,也... and 即使...,也..., all three built on the same "even if...still..." template.

examples.hanzi: 即便你不同意，我也要这样做。
examples.pinyin: Jíbiàn nǐ bù tóngyì, wǒ yě yào zhèyàng zuò.
examples.english: Even if you don't agree, I'm going to do it.

examples.hanzi: 即便再忙，他也会给妈妈打电话。
examples.pinyin: Jíbiàn zài máng, tā yě huì gěi māma dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: No matter how busy he is, he calls his mom.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 钟; mirrors were polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 镜 is jìng; 竟 also sounds out 境 jìng.

example.hanzi: 他戴着一副眼镜。
example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yí fù yǎnjìng.
example.english: He is wearing a pair of glasses.
example.fact: 眼镜 pairs 眼 ("eye") with 镜 ("mirror," built on the metal radical 钅, since early mirrors were polished bronze) — literally "eye mirror," the same logic behind English "looking glass" — and its measure word is 副 ("a pair, a set"), the same classifier used for gloves and a deck of playing cards.

examples.hanzi: 我的眼镜不见了，你看到了吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yǎnjìng bú jiàn le, nǐ kàndào le ma?
examples.english: My glasses are missing; have you seen them?

examples.hanzi: 看书时间长了，我得换一副新眼镜。
examples.pinyin: Kàn shū shíjiān cháng le, wǒ děi huàn yí fù xīn yǎnjìng.
examples.english: I've been reading for a long time and need to get a new pair of glasses.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 伸 is a person stretching out.
申 (shēn) — same sound: 伸 shēn. 申 also sounds out 神 shén and 绅 shēn.

example.hanzi: 请把手伸出来。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shǒu shēn chūlái.
example.english: Please stretch out your hand.
example.fact: 伸 means to stretch or extend: 伸手 (reach out a hand), 伸懒腰 (to stretch lazily). The idiom 能屈能伸 means being able to bend and to stretch, that is, flexible and resilient in good and bad times.

examples.hanzi: 小猫伸了个懒腰。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo shēn le ge lǎnyāo.
examples.english: The kitten stretched.

examples.hanzi: 他伸手去拿桌上的杯子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn shǒu qù ná zhuōzi shang de bēizi.
examples.english: He reached out for the cup on the table.

components.note: 音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢听音乐。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng yīnyuè.
example.english: I like listening to music.
example.fact: 音 means sound, especially pitch and pronunciation: 音乐 (music), 发音 (pronunciation), 口音 (accent), 拼音 (pinyin, 'spell-sound'). 声音 is the everyday word for sound or voice.

examples.hanzi: 这里的声音太大了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèli de shēngyīn tài dà le.
examples.english: The sound here is too loud.

examples.hanzi: 请把音量调小一点。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yīnliàng tiáo xiǎo yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please turn the volume down a little.

components.note: 心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.
亡 (wáng) is a close sound clue for wàng; it also sounds out 忘 wàng (forget) and 网 wǎng.
月 (moon) — to gaze up at the moon, so to look into the distance, then to hope.

example.hanzi: 她的愿望是环游世界。
example.pinyin: Tā de yuànwàng shì huányóu shìjiè.
example.english: Her wish is to travel around the world.
example.fact: 愿 (built from 心, "heart," plus a phonetic 原) contributes "a heartfelt wish," and 望 pictures someone gazing up at the moon 月 in the distance, "to hope, to gaze toward" — 愿望 fuses wishing with gazing toward into a noun for a hope one holds and looks forward to, stronger and more aspirational than the plain verb 想要 ("to want").

examples.hanzi: 我最大的愿望是和家人在一起。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì dà de yuànwàng shì hé jiārén zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: My biggest wish is to be together with my family.

examples.hanzi: 祝你的愿望都能实现！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ de yuànwàng dōu néng shíxiàn!
examples.english: I hope all your wishes come true!

components.note: 尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.
页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 题, 额, 顺; 顶 is the top of the head, hence any top.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 顶 dǐng is close to 订 dìng and 钉 dīng.

example.hanzi: 雨落在屋顶上,发出轻轻的声音。
example.pinyin: Yǔ luò zài wūdǐng shàng, fāchū qīngqīng de shēngyīn.
example.english: Rain fell on the roof, making a soft sound.
example.fact: 顶 already means "the very top" on its own — the top of a head, a mountain, a container — so 屋顶 ("roof") is transparently "the top of the house," the same 顶 that also gives 山顶 ("mountaintop") and 头顶 ("the top of one's head").

examples.hanzi: 小鸟站在屋顶上唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo zhàn zài wūdǐng shang chàng gē.
examples.english: A little bird is standing on the roof singing.

examples.hanzi: 这座房子的屋顶需要修理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò fángzi de wūdǐng xūyào xiūlǐ.
examples.english: The roof of this house needs repair.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.
木 (wood) — beds were wooden frames; 木 is the radical of trees and wooden things like 桌 table and 椅 chair.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上七点起床。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at seven every morning.
example.fact: 起床 literally combines 起 ("to rise," the same 起 seen in 起来 and 一起 in the pilot batch) with 床 ("bed") for "to rise from bed" — its natural opposite is 上床 ("to go to bed," literally "to get onto the bed"), a matched pair built the same simple way.

examples.hanzi: 明天要早起，我六点起床。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yào zǎo qǐ, wǒ liù diǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.english: I have to get up early tomorrow; I'm getting up at six.

examples.hanzi: 孩子赖床，不愿意起床。
examples.pinyin: Háizi làichuáng, bú yuànyì qǐchuáng.
examples.english: The child lingers in bed and doesn't want to get up.

components.note: 兔 — a pictograph of a rabbit: long ears on top and a short dot of a tail; compare 免 without the dot.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 花园里有一只白色的兔子。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ yǒu yì zhī báisè de tùzi.
example.english: There is a white rabbit in the garden.
example.fact: 子 in 兔子 is a light, semantically empty noun suffix rather than a meaningful "child" — the same suffix pattern seen in 孩子 in the pilot batch, though there 子 also happens to independently mean "child," while here in 兔子 it is purely grammatical filler with no connection to baby rabbits.

examples.hanzi: 兔子喜欢吃胡萝卜。
examples.pinyin: Tùzi xǐhuan chī húluóbo.
examples.english: Rabbits like to eat carrots.

examples.hanzi: 我给孩子买了一只兔子当宠物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi háizi mǎi le yì zhī tùzi dāng chǒngwù.
examples.english: I bought a rabbit as a pet for my child.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.hanzi: 这场大赛吸引了很多观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dàsài xīyǐn le hěn duō guānzhòng.
example.english: This grand competition attracted a lot of spectators.
example.fact: 大赛 pairs 大 (“big”) directly with 赛 (“to compete, contest”) to mean a large-scale, high-stakes competition — distinguishing it from a plain 比赛 (“match, competition”), 大赛 signals something like a national or international tournament, on the scale of a World Cup or Olympics.

examples.hanzi: 他在全国编程大赛中拿了奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài quánguó biānchéng dàsài zhōng ná le jiǎng.
examples.english: He won a prize in the national programming contest.

examples.hanzi: 学校下个月要举办歌唱大赛。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xià ge yuè yào jǔbàn gēchàng dàsài.
examples.english: The school will hold a singing contest next month.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 这家公司很重视自己的形象。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī hěn zhòngshì zìjǐ de xíngxiàng.
example.english: This company places great importance on its own image.
example.fact: 形 (built from 开 “a gap or opening” plus 彡 “streaks of light” — light and pattern passing through an opening) and 象 (originally a pictograph of an elephant's trunk and ears, later broadened to “likeness, appearance”) combine into something like “shape and likeness,” giving 形象 its modern sense of a public or mental “image.”

examples.hanzi: 他在同学们心中的形象一直很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài tóngxuémen xīnzhōng de xíngxiàng yìzhí hěn hǎo.
examples.english: His image in his classmates' eyes has always been good.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事里的老人形象非常生动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi lǐ de lǎorén xíngxiàng fēicháng shēngdòng.
examples.english: The old man in this story is vividly portrayed.

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 我们要学会全面地看待事物。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuéhuì quánmiàn de kàndài shìwù.
example.english: We need to learn to look at things comprehensively.
example.fact: 事物 is more abstract than 东西 (“thing,” a concrete physical object) — 事物 covers both tangible objects and intangible matters or phenomena, which is why it shows up constantly in philosophy and formal writing where 东西 would sound too casual.

examples.hanzi: 孩子对新事物总是充满好奇。
examples.pinyin: Háizi duì xīn shìwù zǒngshì chōngmǎn hàoqí.
examples.english: Children are always curious about new things.

examples.hanzi: 随着时间过去，事物也在不断变化。
examples.pinyin: Suízhe shíjiān guòqù, shìwù yě zài búduàn biànhuà.
examples.english: As time passes, things keep changing.

components.note: 衣 (clothing, cloth) — clothes and cloth: 装, 被, 衬; 袋 is a bag made of cloth.
代 (dài) sounds exactly like 袋; also in 贷 dài.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她把苹果放进了袋子里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ píngguǒ fàng jìn le dàizi lǐ.
example.english: She put the apples into the bag.
example.fact: 代 (dài, “generation, to substitute”) supplies 袋's sound almost perfectly, while 衣 (“clothing, cloth”) marks its semantic category — a small reminder that early bags in China were most often sewn from cloth rather than made of other materials.

examples.hanzi: 这个袋子太小，装不下这么多东西。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàizi tài xiǎo, zhuāng bú xià zhème duō dōngxi.
examples.english: This bag is too small to hold so many things.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一个塑料袋子。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge sùliào dàizi.
examples.english: Please give me a plastic bag.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
疒 (sickness) — illness, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain, 疼 ache: madness is an illness.
风 (fēng, wind) gives the exact sound; also in 枫 fēng.

example.hanzi: 他因为压力太大都快发疯了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yālì tài dà dōu kuài fāfēng le.
example.english: He's almost going crazy from all the pressure.
example.fact: 疯 is built from 疒 (“sickness,” the same radical behind 症状's 症, also in this batch) over the phonetic 风 (“wind”) — pairing wind with the sickness radical reflects an old folk belief that madness could be stirred up by a kind of invisible wind disturbing the body.

examples.hanzi: 你再不回来，我就要发疯了！
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài bù huílái, wǒ jiù yào fāfēng le!
examples.english: If you don't come back soon, I'm going to go crazy!

examples.hanzi: 那只狗突然发疯一样地叫了起来。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhī gǒu tūrán fāfēng yíyàng de jiào le qǐlái.
examples.english: The dog suddenly started barking like mad.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 除了周末以外,我每天都要上班。
example.pinyin: Chúle zhōumò yǐwài, wǒ měitiān dōu yào shàngbān.
example.english: Apart from weekends, I have to go to work every day.
example.fact: 以外 usually appears attached after 除了 (“apart from”) in the fixed frame “除了...以外,” even though 除了 alone can already mean “apart from” — a doubling-up of the same logic that mirrors how 因为...所以... keeps both halves in everyday speech.

examples.hanzi: 除了苹果以外，我什么水果都喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Chúle píngguǒ yǐwài, wǒ shénme shuǐguǒ dōu xǐhuan.
examples.english: Besides apples, I like every fruit.

examples.hanzi: 除了他以外，大家都到了。
examples.pinyin: Chúle tā yǐwài, dàjiā dōu dào le.
examples.english: Everyone has arrived except him.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and cords, as in 线 line, 红 red; 绳 is a rope.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 请帮我把绳子系紧。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ shéngzi jì jǐn.
example.english: Please help me tie the rope tight.
example.fact: 绳 pairs the thread radical 纟 with the phonetic 黾 (mǐn, literally “frog, toad”) — an old borrowing purely for sound, since frogs have no real connection to rope-making, and the link has faded further as shéng and mǐn have drifted apart over the centuries.

examples.hanzi: 他用绳子把箱子绑了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shéngzi bǎ xiāngzi bǎng le qǐlái.
examples.english: He tied up the box with a rope.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里跳绳子。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ tiào shéngzi.
examples.english: The children are jumping rope in the yard.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都会读《圣经》。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang dōu huì dú Shèngjīng.
example.english: He reads the Bible every night.
example.fact: 圣 (built from 耳 “ear” and 口 “mouth” above a standing figure — someone who listens and speaks with special insight) plus 经 (“classic text, scripture”) literally suggest “holy scripture” — the same word 圣经 names both the Confucian classics and, in a Christian or Jewish context, the Bible, with context alone usually making clear which is meant.

examples.hanzi: 圣经是世界上发行量最大的书之一。
examples.pinyin: Shèngjīng shì shìjiè shang fāxíng liàng zuì dà de shū zhī yī.
examples.english: The Bible is one of the best-selling books in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这本圣经是奶奶留给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn Shèngjīng shì nǎinai liú gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This Bible was left to me by my grandmother.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这件事成功的可能性很大。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì chénggōng de kěnéngxìng hěn dà.
example.english: The possibility of this succeeding is high.
example.fact: Tacking the suffix 性 (“-ness, -ity”) onto the existing word 可能 (“possible, maybe”) is a fully regular process for turning an adjective into an abstract noun — the same pattern turns 重要 (“important”) into 重要性 (“importance”) and 可靠 (“reliable”) into 可靠性 (“reliability”).

examples.hanzi: 明天下雨的可能性很大。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān xià yǔ de kěnéngxìng hěn dà.
examples.english: There is a high chance of rain tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能排除这种可能性。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng páichú zhè zhǒng kěnéngxìng.
examples.english: We cannot rule out this possibility.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: picking out with the hand.
圣 stands in for 睪 of 擇, a loose sound clue for zé; the original shows up in 泽 zé.

example.hanzi: 面对这种情况,我们别无选择。
example.pinyin: Miànduì zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng, wǒmen bié wú xuǎnzé.
example.english: Faced with this situation, we have no other choice.
example.fact: Unlike many four-character idioms that lean on a classical story or allusion, 别无选择 is built transparently from its own parts — 别 (“other”), 无 (“without”), 选择 (“choice”) — so its meaning can be worked out directly from the pieces, making it one of the more approachable chengyu for learners.

examples.hanzi: 钱花光了，我们别无选择，只能回家。
examples.pinyin: Qián huā guāng le, wǒmen biéwú xuǎnzé, zhǐ néng huí jiā.
examples.english: We ran out of money and had no choice but to go home.

examples.hanzi: 他别无选择，只好接受这份工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā biéwú xuǎnzé, zhǐhǎo jiēshòu zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He had no choice but to accept this job.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 迹 is a footprint, as in 奇迹 miracle.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 迹 is jì; 亦 also sounds out 迹 jì.

example.hanzi: 警察在现场发现了血迹。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài xiànchǎng fāxiàn le xuèjì.
example.english: The police discovered bloodstains at the scene.
example.fact: 迹 pairs the “walking” radical 辶 with the phonetic 亦 (yì) to literally mean “a trace left by walking” — 血迹 extends that same image to blood left behind as a mark or trail, the logic behind other 迹-words like 足迹 (“footprint”) and 痕迹 (“trace, mark”).

examples.hanzi: 地板上有一些血迹，需要擦干净。
examples.pinyin: Dìbǎn shang yǒu yìxiē xuèjì, xūyào cā gānjìng.
examples.english: There are some bloodstains on the floor that need to be wiped off.

examples.hanzi: 衬衫上的血迹很难洗掉。
examples.pinyin: Chènshān shang de xuèjì hěn nán xǐ diào.
examples.english: The bloodstains on the shirt are hard to wash out.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的菜非常美味。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài fēicháng měiwèi.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is extremely delicious.
example.fact: 美 (built from 羊, here representing an ornate headdress, plus 大, a person with arms outstretched — someone wearing a fine headdress was seen as “beautiful”) pairs with 味 (“taste, flavor”) to form 美味, quite literally “beautiful taste” — a word that works as both an adjective (“delicious”) and a noun (“a delicacy”).

examples.hanzi: 奶奶做的饭菜非常美味。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò de fàncài fēicháng měiwèi.
examples.english: The food Grandma makes is delicious.

examples.hanzi: 这里有许多当地的美味可以尝尝。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu xǔduō dāngdì de měiwèi kěyǐ chángchang.
examples.english: There are many local delicacies to try here.
